name: Row Commands
tagline: Open, launch or delete from the row itself — plus commands of your own, Activate and Deactivate, and selection.
summary:
Puts commands at the end of every row of a view, with no ribbon customisation: **Open** goes to the record's form, **Open link** follows an address held in a column you map, and **Delete** asks for confirmation first.

- **Your own commands** (new in 0.3.0): buttons you describe in JSON, each setting columns on the row or reporting a press to a form script
- **Activate and Deactivate** on each row and over a selection (new in 0.3.0)
- Optional row selection, to act on several rows with one confirmation
- Delete and writes offered only to users whose roles allow them
- Resizable columns, remembered per user and view

limitations: Open calls context.navigation.openForm, as on a form, and refreshes the view when the form closes. There is no form behind the demo, so the event log under the demo names the record that would have opened. The invokedRecordId, invokedCommand and invokeCount outputs still update, which is the value a canvas app would react to, and it is the same thing the control reports on a real form. Switch the toolbar's host to Canvas app and Open takes the dataset's own openDatasetItem instead, which raises OnSelect there, as the event log shows; a canvas app publishes openForm and refuses it, so the control does not ask.

Delete works against the demo's stand-in Dataverse. The control asks first with context.navigation.openConfirmDialog, drawn inside the demo, and only on Delete calls context.webAPI.deleteRecord and refreshes, so the row leaves the table; Cancel leaves it alone and says so. Nothing leaves the browser: Reset or a reload puts the rows back. A refused delete shows too: the stand-in refuses Northwind Traders, the way a plugin would on a real environment, so deleting it opens the error dialog a real form opens on a failure, with the reason under Details, and the row stays. Delete selected over a selection that includes it deletes the rest and names Northwind Traders in one error dialog. In a canvas app, which reports no organisation URL, the control draws no Delete at all: switch the toolbar's host to Canvas app to see the rows without it.

The website addresses in the fixture are example.com placeholders, so following one leads nowhere. What is real is which rows offer the link and which do not: the address is read from a bound column, checked against http and https, and a row whose column is empty gets no button. One record in the fixture has no address for that reason.

Paging and sorting work against the fixture. A header click sorts the whole fixture on the next fetch, the way a real view sorts on the server across every page, and goes back to page one. The Compact preset asks for four rows a page, so its eight rows make two pages. The page size is still a request: a real view may clamp it, and the ceiling is 250.

Selection works here as a checkbox column and a bar, and a tick survives a re-render: change a property or the theme and it stays. With Delete switched on the bar offers Delete selected: one confirmation for the lot, then one deleteRecord per row, one after another, and a single refresh at the end. A sort or a new page size clears the selection on purpose, because it names rows the reader may no longer see. The subgrid command bar that acts on a selection on a real form is part of the form, not of the control, so it is not here.

Resizing works for real. Drag a column edge, or tab to it and press the arrow keys. Whether the width is remembered across a reload depends on whether this page may use the browser's storage; where it may not, the width lasts until the page is reloaded, which is the control's real behaviour on a browser that refuses storage.

Your own commands are given to the demo as JSON in the Your commands property. On a form that property can also name a web resource holding the JSON, which a form needs once the JSON passes 100 characters, the most the form designer accepts in a property. The demo has no web resources, so a name there says it was not found.

A command that writes, and Activate or Deactivate, writes to the demo's stand-in Dataverse through context.webAPI.updateRecord, as on a form, and the view refreshes to show it. Reset puts the rows back. The demo describes the Industry and Status choices but not their default status reasons, so Activate and Deactivate send the state alone here; on a form the control reads each state's default reason and sends it beside the state.

Escalate reports on the outputs (invokedCommand, invokedRecordId, invokeCount) and raises onRowCommand, both shown in the event log under the demo. On a model-driven form a form script reads the outputs with addOnOutputChange; onRowCommand was not delivered to a form script on a subgrid when measured, so the docs lead with the outputs.

The demo runs as a subgrid on a contact's form, which is why Escalate shows: a command that only reports a press is left off a main grid, where nothing can hear it. Industry is a column of the demo's view; on a form, the control fetches a column a command writes when the view lacks it, without drawing it.

presets.name: Open and open link
presets.description: The shipped defaults: every row can be opened, and a row with a website address can have it launched. This is what a maker gets by dropping the control on a view and mapping one column.

presets.name: Your own commands
presets.description: New in 0.3.0: commands described in JSON. Mark as Logistics and Accounting set Industry on the row (Accounting asks first); Escalate only reports the press, for a form script or a formula. Tick rows to run them over a selection.

presets.name: Activate and Deactivate
presets.description: New in 0.3.0: Deactivate on each active row, Activate on the inactive one, and both over a selection, which skips the rows already in that state. The state is read from each row and written back in one update.

presets.name: Select rows, resize columns
presets.description: New in 0.2.0: a checkbox per row, a header that selects the page, and a bar counting the selection, with Delete selected to remove them together. Drag a column edge, or tab to it and use the arrow keys, and the column follows.

presets.name: Links only
presets.description: Open switched off, for a view where the record is not the point — vendors somebody only ever visits the website of. It is named Hide rather than Show because a Yes/No property has no way to default to Yes.

presets.name: Delete, with confirmation
presets.description: Delete switched on: every row gets one, and pressing it asks first. Confirm and the row leaves the table; Cancel and nothing happens. Northwind Traders is refused, so it opens the error dialog instead. Reset puts the rows back.

presets.name: A shorter page
presets.description: Four rows per page. The page size is a request rather than an instruction — the platform may clamp it, and the ceiling is 250 — so on a real view this is what the control asks for rather than what it necessarily gets.
